committee.name: Velox Governance Committee
committee.mission: Govern Velox as a capital allocation machine: preserve edge, control drawdown, prevent ungoverned complexity, and scale only what proves durable expectancy after friction.
committee.doctrine: Do not optimize for activity, novelty, or sophistication. Optimize for durable net expectancy, controlled losses, reliable execution, honest attribution, and disciplined capital scaling.

roles.title: Builder
roles.summary: Owns implementation clarity, operational safety, and rollback realism.
required_questions: What changed?
What system layer does it touch?
What can break operationally?
How do we roll it back?

roles.title: Quant Reviewer
roles.summary: Owns statistical honesty, regime fit, and edge validation by book.
required_questions: Does this improve expectancy or just activity?
Which books or regimes should benefit?
What evidence would falsify the claim?
Is the sample size good enough to believe this?

roles.title: Portfolio Manager
roles.summary: Owns book lifecycle, capital routing, and portfolio-level judgment.
required_questions: Which books deserve more or less capital?
How does this affect concentration and cross-book exposure?
Should this book be incubation, active, scaled, probation, or retired?
What should happen to capital if the change underperforms?

roles.title: Risk Committee
roles.summary: Owns downside protection, tail-risk skepticism, and de-risking rules.
required_questions: What gets worse if this is wrong?
Could this increase tail losses, churn, or hidden fragility?
Should this be capped, shadowed, or rejected?
What kill-switch or rollback condition applies?

roles.title: Outside Critic
roles.summary: Owns pressure-testing the narrative and calling out when architecture outruns proof.
required_questions: Are we fixing the right bottleneck?
Is complexity outrunning evidence?
Should we prune instead of add?
Is the story stronger than the data?

roles.title: Human Chairman
roles.summary: Owns final approval, capital/risk escalation, and weekly governance review.
required_questions: What are we optimizing for this week?
What should be approved, capped, or rejected?
Which books earn more or less capital now?
What must be rolled back or put on probation?
